R9408.summary: Jörg Weinmeister (signed in cipher) to the Dukes of Bavaria from Ofen, 8 Feb 1534, with Latin clear passages: his mission, the Turk's power and money, mining (Schmaltz, Reinhart), Katzianer before Kaschau, the priest-bishop Emericus and bad coin with the dukes' stamp; a separate news page on Emperor Sigmund, Constantinople and Syria.
R9408.en:
[to] report to the Germans what a war [?] experienced [?] happens [?] [?] [?] here [?] [?] [?] in [?] against comfort,
what has hitherto happened from the Germans [?] by the Turk, and that all the world knows [?] [?] it is not hidden that
he [?] because [?] [?] seen [?] [?] some [?] [?] Turks' [s]oldiery «as ten and twenty yea[rs]» [?] [?] [?] have beaten,
which has brought little use, as Your [Princely Graces] may consider for yourselves [?], and still both unwillingly a
long memory. [Your Princely Graces] [know] what Emperor Sigismund, who ruled the whole of Hungary and laid it waste,
and was besides King of Bohemia and Roman Emperor, and who led over six thousand men from Germany alone [?]

R9409.summary: German intelligence report of early 1534: Ferdinand and the confederation, the Turkish embassy, Pressburg, Katzianer and Majláth in Transylvania, Késmárk, Poland and Muscovy, with numbered articles on mining (Antoni Slesinger, Schmaltz, Freiberger, gold-exchangers) and a postscript on the Reichstag.

R9410.summary: German letter to the dukes dated the first of April 1535: a treaty, the King of France, and holding together as brothers against the Turks.

R9413.summary: Letters of a Bavarian agent to the dukes, 7 June and July 1534, addressed to secretary Waisenfelder: Cornelius, the French orator Antonius Rincon at Constantinople, Katzianer, the bishop of Wardein before Hunyad, the Württemberg war, an ore sample from near Ofen, the Turk's fleet and the Pressburg diet.

R9427.summary: German newsletter to a duke, 15/21/24 April 1534 with a postscript of 25 April: the Württemberg affair (the Bund, the dukes of Württemberg, the Landgrave), Ferdinand, and a provost-priest who married and was imprisoned; lines 1-10 carry a contemporary gloss.
